notes: LAYER 1 — identification: a three-slab glass desk; one horizontal top plus two full-height vertical end panels, joined by four metal L-brackets. No stretcher, no apron, no drawers visible.

LAYER 2 — silhouette: bounding volume 1.40 m wide × 0.74 m high × 0.70 m deep; footprint is two thin rectangles ≈0.015 m × 0.70 m set 1.28 m apart, not a solid rectangle. Three box primitives suffice: top slab 1.40 × 0.015 × 0.70, and two panels 0.015 × 0.725 × 0.60 each. Bilateral symmetry about the width centre plane; also near-symmetric front-to-back, so the back face is assumed to mirror the front.

LAYER 2 — proportions against the 1.40 m width reference: depth 0.50×, height 0.53×, panel depth ≈0.43× (0.60 m, i.e. shorter than the top's 0.70 m depth so the top overhangs front and back by ≈0.05 m), panel thickness ≈0.011× (0.015 m), top overhang past each panel ≈0.04× (0.05 m).

LAYER 3 — macro parts (3): (a) top slab, (b) left side panel, (c) right side panel. Meso parts: four L-brackets (two per panel, at the top front and top back corners of each panel's inner face), four polished slab edges, four polished panel edges, two foot-pad pairs. Micro: bracket fixing bosses/screw heads, bracket arm tapers, edge polish bands, the inset glide buttons.

LAYER 4 — relationships: the top slab RESTS ON the upper edge of each side panel as a butt joint, glass-to-glass, with no visible gasket; each L-bracket is BOLTED through the side panel's inner face and its horizontal arm is BOLTED up into (or bonded against) the underside of the top slab, so the brackets carry the moment of the joint; the top slab's underside is FLUSH with the panel top edges along their 0.015 m width; the top OVERHANGS each panel outward by ≈0.05 m and forward/backward by ≈0.05 m; the glide pads are INSET into the bottom edge of each panel and CONTACT the floor, so the glass edge itself stands ≈0.002 m clear of the floor.

LAYER 5/6 — colour: single hue family throughout, amber-brown at roughly 25–30° hue, mid value, medium-high saturation. Gradient on each side panel outer face, ordered stops: 0.00 (top edge) #C97A3A, 0.55 #A0561F, 1.00 (bottom edge) #7E3F1C. Top slab gradient, front edge to back edge: 0.00 #B0682F, 1.00 #92501F. All glass reads gloss; brackets read satin metallic; the only matte elements are the glide pads.

OBSERVATION vs INFERENCE: observation — the panel faces show a smooth vertical brightness gradient with no visible grain, weave or seam. INFERENCE — the panels are single-piece tinted glass rather than laminated wood or acrylic, and the gradient is transmission through the backdrop plus body tint, not a printed or sprayed fade.

OBSERVATION — the top slab shows one broad soft highlight with no micro-texture. INFERENCE — roughness ≈0.03–0.06 on both glass faces; model as transmissive with IOR ≈1.52 and an amber absorption tint rather than as an opaque brown surface.

OBSERVATION — the far panel's brackets are visible as darkened shapes behind/through the top slab. INFERENCE — the top slab transmits ≈40–55% of light and refracts only slightly, consistent with ≈12–15 mm thickness.

HIDDEN — the back long face of the desk, the underside of the top slab, the inner faces of both side panels below the brackets, and the exact bracket fixing pattern (number of screws, whether through-bolts with bushings) are not visible.

HIDDEN — the right panel is seen nearly edge-on; its bracket pair, edge polish and foot pads are assumed to mirror the left panel under the left-right symmetry assumption for manufactured furniture. No evidence in the photo contradicts this.
UNCERTAIN — two small pale rectangles on the left panel's bottom edge could be glide pads or adhesive-backed labels; modelled here as glides because they sit exactly at the floor contact line.

UNCERTAIN — overall size has no in-frame scale cue; dimensions come from the desk class and from the ≈0.015 m glass thickness read against the panel height (roughly 48:1), giving a working height near 0.74 m.

STUDIO CONTEXT — seamless light-grey sweep, soft top-left key light, faint contact shadow under the near panel only; low confidence on camera placement because the ground shadow is weak and the glass gives no ground-plane anchor.
